claims.text: In-situ heating TEM coupled with HAADF-STEM can reveal atomic-scale thermal behavior in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
The method can directly visualize temperature-induced atomic rearrangements in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
The method can directly visualize temperature-induced phase transformations in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
The AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are a nearly equiatomic high-entropy nanoalloy.
The AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles have a well-ordered structure at room temperature.
A specialized TEM heating stage can gradually and controllably raise the nanoparticle temperature.
The experiment would use controlled, incremental temperature ramps in a high-vacuum TEM environment.
An inert atmosphere may be used if necessary to prevent oxidation.
Increasing temperature may drive phase evolution, defect production, and elemental redistribution in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Heating can induce structural changes such as phase separation or defect creation.
HAADF-STEM provides enhanced atomic-number contrast.
HAADF-STEM can capture heating-induced structural changes in real time with high spatial resolution.
Heating will produce observable temperature-dependent atomic rearrangements and possibly phase transitions or defect formation.
Such changes would indicate increased thermal activation relative to the room-temperature baseline.
At room temperature, Au, Co, Cu, Ni, and Pt are homogeneously and orderly distributed with minimal defects.
Results obtained under TEM vacuum and limited pressure control may not reproduce industrial high-temperature environments.
Electron-beam effects must be managed during the heating experiment.
TEM-based methods have previously been effective for atomic-scale analysis of high-entropy alloys.
The temperature thresholds for observable changes in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are undetermined.
Electron diffraction recorded during heating can be used to detect phase changes.
